name: Glass House
subtitle: Historic Victorian Glass Pavilion
description: The Glass House is Lal Bagh's central jewel, commissioned in 1889 during the administration of John Cameron. Modelled after London's Crystal Palace, it hosts the famous bi-annual flower shows during Republic Day and Independence Day.
historicalFacts: Commissioned in 1889, constructed with iron cast from Macfarlane's Foundry in Glasgow, Scotland.
Stands on the site of Tipu Sultan's original rose garden collection.
Hosts twice-yearly flower shows featuring over 200 varieties of flora.
botanicalNotes: Surrounded by royal palms, Araucaria cookii trees, and curated orchids.

name: Kempegowda Tower
subtitle: 16th-Century Watchtower on Peninsular Gneiss
description: Perched atop a 3,000-million-year-old Peninsular Gneiss rock outcrop, this watchtower is one of four erected by Kempegowda I in 1537 to demarcate the future boundary of Bengaluru city.
historicalFacts: Built by Bengaluru founder Kempegowda I in 1537 AD.
The underlying rock formation is classified as a National Geological Monument by GSI.
Marks the southern boundary prediction of ancient Bengaluru.
botanicalNotes: Surrounded by drought-resistant xerophytic rock flora and ancient cacti species.

name: Old Banyan Tree
subtitle: Centuries-Old Ficus Benghalensis
description: A majestic centuries-old Banyan tree (Ficus benghalensis) featuring a sprawling canopy of prop roots that create a living pillar structure providing shelter to hundreds of native birds and fruit bats.
historicalFacts: Estimated to be over 200 years old, planted during the Hyder Ali era.
Prop roots have rooted into independent secondary trunks over decades.
Serves as a keystone ecological hub within the Lal Bagh botanical sanctuary.
botanicalNotes: Ficus benghalensis with prop roots covering an area exceeding 0.5 acres.

name: The Lake (Lotus Pond)
subtitle: Historic Rainwater Reservoir & Avian Sanctuary
description: Lal Bagh Lake is a historic artificial lake constructed to supply irrigation water to the botanical gardens. It features an island bird sanctuary and lotus cultivation zones.
historicalFacts: Designed during the 18th century to create a self-sustaining irrigation system.
Features a protected central island hosting spot-billed pelicans and cormorants.
Serves as an urban wetland cooling micro-climate.
botanicalNotes: Nelumbo nucifera (sacred lotus), Nymphaea water lilies, and shoreline weeping willows.
